chose: 4.4 step 1: homeInitiative's per-log registration lookup reads a DERIVED registration cache, .sofar/.index/registrations/<slug>.json, maintained by reading only the log's tail. TypeScript first, then the Rust mirror with parity. For every session, the cache holds exactly the answer registrationIn gives: the first line in file order that parses as an object with type session_started, a string session, id and ts, and whose raw text contains that session id (registrationIn's own pre-filter, kept so the answer is identical). It covers complete lines only, and the unterminated last line is always scanned live. The cache is trusted only when the log is unchanged (size and mtimeMs) or has grown past the consumed offset with its last consumed line hashing the same (the check D22's chain-hash snapshots use). Anything else rebuilds from a full scan. registrationIn itself stays the reference, and the scan remains the fallback.
over: Keeping the full-log scan per call. At team100 it reads and decodes 95 MB on every hook and statusline call: 143 ms of a 143 ms cached statusline, relative and under load. Also over a written session-to-slug index, which record-integrity D1 rejected and which this is not.
because: record-integrity D1 rejected a second store WRITTEN at registration, which could desync, needed pruning and meant committing routing state under .sofar/. It also judged the scan cheap at ~350 KB of total logs. This cache is none of the rejected things. It is derived only from the log, and every read re-checks it against the log (so it cannot desync silently). It is gitignored under .sofar/.index like the index tiers (so no Record-layout change). And it is disposable (lost or corrupt means a rescan). The log is still the only truth, as D1 requires. What changed is D1's cost premise: at team100 the scan is the whole remaining cost of the cached statusline and of every hook's resolution.
